subject: Depot transfer manifest & acceptance window — signer cadence and verification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Operations - IronCloud <ops@ironcloud.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Depot transfer manifest & acceptance window — signer cadence and verification

Hi team,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is transfer_manifest_v3.json and the current signer_roster_20270307.csv. We're preparing a sealed delivery to NorthBridge's cold depot the week of Mar 15. Before we lock dates I need confirmation on three items so the audit trail stays clean:

- Acceptance window: we need a 4-hour operator acceptance window where the depot operator will validate signatures and hash sums before activation.
- Signer cadence: a two-person signer model (operator + RedWood on-call) is required for acceptance; we plan to bring a temporary activation token valid for 6 hours.
- Courier SLA: expected handoff ETA and proof-of-delivery format (photo + signed manifest PDF).

Please respond with acceptance of the window and any constraints by EOD Wed (Mar 10). If IronCloud needs a different window, propose alternatives and include expected audit artifacts.

Attachments: transfer_manifest_v3.json (stub, 12KB), signer_roster_20270307.csv (stub, 3KB)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Operations - IronCloud <ops@ironcloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 13:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Depot transfer manifest & acceptance window — signer cadence and verification

Ben —

We can support the 4-hour acceptance window and the two-person signer model. A few clarifying items:

1) Hash verification: we will run SHA256 of the bundle on arrival and provide the hash.txt with signed operator assertion. Please ensure the manifest includes per-file SHA256 values (the v3 manifest looks like it does).
2) Temporary activation token: ops can accept a time-limited token; we recommend 4 hours rather than 6 given our operator shift handovers unless RedWood confirms hardened on-call coverage.
3) Courier proof: we will supply a GPS-tagged photo, the signed manifest PDF (scanned), and a digital courier receipt signed by the depot gate.

We suggest the handoff slot on Tue, Mar 16, 0900-1300 PT. If that works for you we'll schedule the courier and list the operator on the manifest.

— IronCloud Ops (supply team)
From: Mike Tanaka <mike@northbridge.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Operations - IronCloud <ops@ironcloud.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Depot transfer manifest & acceptance window — signer cadence and verification

Ben / IronCloud —

NorthBridge confirms availability for Tue, Mar 16 0900-1300 PT. A couple of operational constraints from our side:

- Depot operator shift change is at 1100; so we need the acceptance handshake to complete by 1045 to avoid handoff ambiguity.
- We require the temporary activation token to be generated as a split secret: one part given to the depot operator, one held by Redwood on-call. That way neither party can activate unilaterally.
- For our audit we also need a short video (30–60s) of the operator performing the hash verification step; this stays internal to NorthBridge but must be referenced in the signed manifest.

If you can issue the token as a split (2-of-2) and shorten to 4-hour validity, we can proceed.

— Mike Tanaka, Program Lead — NorthBridge Systems
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mike Tanaka <mike@northbridge.io>, Operations - IronCloud <ops@ironcloud.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Depot transfer manifest & acceptance window — signer cadence and verification

Thanks Mike — that's all reasonable. Quick notes / decisions:

- We'll change token validity to 4 hours and produce it as a split 2-of-2 secret. Redwood on-call will hold one share; the depot operator will hold the other.
- We'll annotate transfer_manifest_v3.json with per-file SHA256 (I attached a small manifest diff in drive; link in related_links).
- Acceptance handshake must complete by 1045 on Mar 16; IronCloud please confirm operator arrival and readiness by EOD Mar 15.
- Jonas: can you draft the acceptance checklist PDF with the explicit steps (photo, video, hash file, signed manifest)? I attached depot_acceptance_checklist.pdf as a starter — please iterate.

Ben
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mike Tanaka <mike@northbridge.io>, Operations - IronCloud <ops@ironcloud.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Depot transfer manifest & acceptance window — signer cadence and verification

Folks —

I've updated depot_acceptance_checklist.pdf (v2) and exported signer_roster_20270307.csv -> signer_roster_20270307_signed.csv (stub). Checklist highlights:

- Pre-arrival: verify courier manifest IDs, confirm operator identity via gov ID and employer badge.
- Arrival: photograph sealed container (2 angles), confirm courier receipt, scan manifest into depot system.
- Verification: run sha256sum for each artifact, save <filename>.sha256, record operator assertion and timestamp.
- Activation sequence: 1) Operator uploads .sha256 and manifest; 2) Redwood on-call publishes their split share to rendezvous server; 3) Operator uses local tool to assemble token and perform activation; 4) Operator records 30–60s verification video and links it in manifest.
- Escalation: if any mismatch, immediate quarantine and notify RedWood escalation alias (esc-redwood@redwood.com).

Attachments: depot_acceptance_checklist_v2.pdf (stub), signer_roster_20270307_signed.csv (stub)

Jonas Weber
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
